tags: [bees, health]
date: 2024-06-10
---
Stung on the inside of the left wrist on 8 June 2024 while lifting a frame out of Primrose, through the gap between glove and cuff. Scraped the sting out with a fingernail within ten seconds. By the evening the swelling ran to the elbow, hot and itchy, and by the morning my watch wouldn't go on. No trouble breathing, no hives elsewhere, so a large local reaction rather than anything systemic. Took cetirizine 10 mg, ice pack in a tea towel, arm up on a cushion. Saw Dr Anand at the Bovey Tracey surgery on the 10th: she said these reactions are common in older keepers and don't usually mean the next one will be worse, but prescribed two adrenaline pens anyway (Jext 300, expiry 03/2026) and said to keep one in the bee box. The pollen season makes my eyes worse every May regardless, see [[Seasonal allergies]]. Now I tape the cuffs, and the burn I got off the vaporiser in December is a separate story in [[Oxalic acid vapour dosing]].
